subject: Re: MAP draft & POC environment dependencies (VPC, SSO, IP allowlist)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@acme.com>
Cc: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft & POC environment dependencies (VPC, SSO, IP allowlist)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (attached) focused on the POC environment setup. High level items we discussed:

- Goal: 2-week POC to validate LLM inference latency/throughput against ACME query mix, target start: 2026-06-08, target close: 2026-06-22.
- POC environment dependencies (POC milestone "env ready"):
  - VPC peering (ACME VPC <-> Redwood POC VPC)
  - IP allowlist / firewall rules (Outbound and inbound as needed)
  - SSO / SAML metadata for test users (IdP -> Redwood)
  - Secrets & KMS access model (how keys will be provided or whether Redwood KMS used)

I've attached a MAP draft (MAP-draft-v1.pdf) with milestone owners and proposed dates. Action items to unblock the env milestone:

1) ACME: Provide VPC peering contact + VPC IDs (owner: Alex) — target 2026-05-26
2) ACME: Share IP ranges to allow to/from Redwood (owner: Priya) — target 2026-05-26
3) ACME: Share SAML IdP metadata and test user(s) for SSO (owner: Priya) — target 2026-05-29
4) Redwood: Provide firewall rules and KMS integration notes, and will propose if we need customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed secrets (owner: Marissa / Nikhil) — target 2026-05-28

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 274KB)]

Next steps: if Alex/Priya can confirm owners and dates above, I'll update the MAP and send a calendar invite for a short technical sync (30m) with your infra/security folks.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- The proposed POC window (6/8–6/22) looks fine, but procurement may need a week lead for access. We can try to keep infra tasks on your timeline.
- I'll own the VPC peering work but will need our cloud networking engineer to be on the tech sync.
- Priya will own SSO and IP allowlists; she may loop in InfoSec for approval on IP ranges.

Can you confirm if Redwood needs a VPN endpoint or just VPC peering and public IP allowlist? Also please share the minimal firewall ports/protocols we need to open so I can pass to our networking team.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform — ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-23T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & POC environment dependencies (VPC, SSO, IP allowlist)

Hi Alex — thanks. Short answers:

- Preferred: VPC peering (private) + IP allowlist for control-plane endpoints. VPN is optional; we can support either, but peering will give lower latency during the POC.
- Minimal egress/ingress: outbound TCP 443 to our control-plane and inference endpoints; we'll provide a short CSV with IP ranges. For the data plane (inference) we may request whitelisting of Redwood inference subnet or allowlist our NAT IPs listed in the CSV.
- KMS/secrets: if you want customer-managed keys (CMK) we can integrate via standard KMS wrapping; otherwise Redwood-managed secrets are OK for the POC. Nikhil will outline the exact steps.

I've updated the MAP with clarified owners and tentative dates. Pushing the env-ready milestone target to 2026-06-01 to account for procurement lead time — still targeting POC start 2026-06-08.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme-firewall-allowlist.csv (text/csv, 2KB)]

I'll schedule a 30-min technical sync for next week — proposing 2026-05-27 10:00 PT. If that works for Alex/Priya, please accept; otherwise propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa —

Quick notes from InfoSec / infra:
- I'll own the IP allowlist and will send the official CSV by 2026-05-26. For now, attached is a working set of NAT egress IPs we can whitelist during the POC.
- SAML metadata: we can provide IdP metadata (SAML 2.0) — our SSO admin will generate a test SP configuration and share metadata by 2026-05-28. We can provide 2 test users in the ACME dev group.
- KMS: InfoSec prefers customer-managed keys for production, but for the POC they are fine using Redwood-managed secrets. We will decide by the end of POC.

InfoSec contact for the tech sync: Jordan Blake (jordan.blake@acme.com). Please include them on the invite.

--Priya

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MAP draft & POC environment dependencies (VPC, SSO, IP allowlist)

Looping in a couple implementation specifics from the Redwood side so ACME knows what to expect on the tech sync: 

- VPC peering: we'll provide a CloudFormation/Terraform snippet and the Redwood VPC IDs; peering is straightforward but ACME's routing table will need an entry for our subnets.
- IPs/ports: for control-plane ops we require outbound HTTPS (443) to the control-plane; for inference traffic (data plane) we recommend peering. If peering not possible, we'll provide fixed NAT IPs to allowlist.
- SAML/SSO: we support SAML 2.0 IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. We'll need the IdP metadata XML and a test account with SSO access for validation.
- Secrets/KMS: for POC we can use Redwood-managed secrets. If ACME prefers CMK, we'll coordinate a short HLD for key wrapping (we support AWS KMS & GCP KMS via key-wrap).

Link to our POC onboarding doc: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/poc-environment (will include the snippets above).

I'll be on the technical sync. Marissa — please send the invite to Alex, Priya, Jordan Blake, and optionally the ACME networking engineer.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Staff Engineer, Infra Integrations
nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
